facts.label: Escolher o trem
facts.sub: Pergunta útil na estação: qual trem, qual plataforma e quantas paradas até o seu destino.

facts.label: Local ou expresso
facts.sub: Em muitos sistemas de metrô, trens “local” param em todas as estações e trens “express” pulam várias. Antes de entrar, confira o letreiro do trem e a direção, como “Uptown” ou “Downtown”.

facts.label: Pagar a passagem
facts.sub: Em muitas cidades você paga com cartão de transporte, cartão de crédito ou aplicativo, encostando no leitor da catraca. Os preços e o sistema mudam de cidade para cidade, então vale olhar as instruções na estação.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

pages.title: My first subway ride in New York · 1/3
paragraphs: Yesterday I took the subway in New York for the first time. I was very nervous. The station was big, loud and full of people. I wanted to go to Brooklyn, but I did not know which train to take.

I saw a man with a map and said, “**Excuse me, which train goes to Brooklyn?**” “**Take the number two train**,” he said. “Where is the platform?” I asked. “**Go down the stairs. It’s on the left**,” he answered.

pages.title: My first subway ride in New York · 2/3
paragraphs: I went down the stairs and found the platform. A train came with a loud noise. I asked a woman, “**How many stops?**” She said, “**Four stops. Get off at Atlantic Avenue**.” I thanked her and got on the train.
The train was a local, so it stopped at every station. It was slow, but I did not mind. I counted the stops: one, two, three, four. A voice said, “The next stop is Atlantic Avenue.”

pages.title: My first subway ride in New York · 3/3
paragraphs: I got off, went up the stairs and walked into the sun. A smiling man at the exit said, “**Have a good trip!**” It was a small moment, but I felt very happy.
Now I know that the subway is not scary. You can always ask for help, and most people are kind.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em “Get off at”, três palavrinhas terminam e começam com vogal ou som leve, e no inglês falado se juntam num bloco só. Quem separa as palavras costuma não entender o anúncio ou a resposta rápida.
pages.how: Ligue o /t/ de “get” ao “off”: o /t/ fica rápido, quase um /d/ (“ge-doff”). Depois ligue “off” a “at”: “gedoffat”. Dê a força em “off” e deixe o resto leve.
pages.tip: Diga a frase bem devagar batendo palmas só em “off” e “At-lan-tic”, depois acelere sem parar entre as palavras.
